# Android Platform (Jetpack Compose / Material 3 Expressive): Interaction & Accessibility

Self-contained. The skill's rules, then this topic, then anything it relies on from other skills.

## Skill rules

Current stable Android. Kotlin. Compose only. Material 3 Expressive (M3E) is an evolution of Material You, not a replacement: spring motion, emphasized type, shape morphing, and a revised component set on the same token system. Motion, type, and shape work together. One without the others looks like M3E but doesn't feel like it. Support dynamic color, with a brand palette as the fallback.

Design values follow m3.material.io. API names follow AndroidX. Load only the reference file the task needs.

| Topic | Reference |
| --- | --- |
| Gradle setup, theme wiring, color roles, dynamic color, contrast, elevation | [reference/theme-and-color.md](theme-and-color.md) |
| Type scale, Roboto Flex, shape scale, shape morphing, `MotionScheme`, reduce motion | [reference/typography-shape-motion.md](typography-shape-motion.md) |
| Spacing, M3E components, insets, adaptive layout, Navigation 3, predictive back | [reference/components-and-navigation.md](components-and-navigation.md) |
| Ripple, state layers, haptics, touch targets, semantics, contrast | [reference/interaction-and-accessibility.md](interaction-and-accessibility.md) |
| Canvas, mesh gradients, AGSL, `RenderEffect`, blur, rich text | [reference/custom-rendering.md](custom-rendering.md) |

### Version Snapshot

As of 2026-11-10. This is the only place the skill pins versions. Before pinning anything, check the [BOM mapping](https://developer.android.com/develop/ui/compose/bom/bom-mapping) and the [material3 release notes](https://developer.android.com/jetpack/androidx/releases/compose-material3). If they disagree with this table, they win.

| Thing | Current |
| --- | --- |
| Platform | Android 17, API 37. Google Play requires targetSdk 36+ |
| Kotlin | 2.4.21 |
| Compose BOM | 2026.09.00: Compose 1.12.1, `material3` 1.4.0, `material3-adaptive-navigation-suite` 1.4.0, adaptive 1.3.0 |
| `material3` with M3E | 1.5.0-rc01, in no BOM yet, built against Compose 1.12 |
| Navigation 3 | 1.2.1 (`navigation-compose` 2.10.2 still maintained) |
| Other | `navigationevent` 1.2.0, `activity` 1.13.0, `window` 1.5.1, `graphics-shapes` 1.1.0 |

**M3E needs `material3` 1.5.0. That's a release candidate, and it isn't in the stable BOM.** `material3` 1.4.0 has no M3E API at all, not even behind an opt-in. Getting M3E means pinning 1.5.0 on top of the BOM (see theme-and-color.md). That's a decision. Raise it before building anything.

- **In 1.4.0 (plain BOM):** baseline M3 components, `ShortNavigationBar`, `WideNavigationRail`, `NavigationSuiteScaffold`, surface container and fixed color roles, `ripple()`.
- **1.5.0, stable:** `MaterialExpressiveTheme`, `expressiveLightColorScheme()`, `MotionScheme` / `MaterialTheme.motionScheme`, emphasized type styles (`titleLargeEmphasized`...), `Typography(fontFamily)`, shape tokens `largeIncreased` / `extraLargeIncreased` / `extraExtraLarge`, `ButtonShapes` and the `shapes` parameter on buttons, `ToggleButton`, `ButtonGroup`, `SplitButtonLayout`, `HorizontalFloatingToolbar` / `VerticalFloatingToolbar`, `FloatingActionButtonMenu`, `Modifier.animateFloatingActionButton`, `LinearWavyProgressIndicator` / `CircularWavyProgressIndicator`, `MediumFlexibleTopAppBar` / `LargeFlexibleTopAppBar`.
- **1.5.0, `@OptIn(ExperimentalMaterial3ExpressiveApi::class)`:** `LoadingIndicator`, `ContainedLoadingIndicator`, `MaterialShapes`, `RoundedPolygon.toShape()`.
- **Don't exist:** `expressiveDarkColorScheme()`, a composable named `SplitButton`, a plain `FloatingToolbar`.

By targetSdk: 35 enforces edge-to-edge. 36 removes the opt-out, turns predictive back on (`onBackPressed` and `KEYCODE_BACK` are no longer delivered), and ignores orientation and resizability locks on displays 600dp and wider. 37 removes the opt-out for that last one.

### Platform Visual Signature

A correct Android / M3E design looks like Google made it. If it reads as iOS or as a website, it's wrong.

- Navigation bar at the bottom with 3-5 labeled destinations on compact widths. Navigation rail (3-7 destinations, optional FAB) on wider windows
- Edge-to-edge: system bars are transparent and content draws behind them
- Dynamic color: the primary hue changes per device
- Roboto Flex or Roboto throughout. Not SF Pro, not Inter. Roboto is the M3 default. I use Roboto Flex for its variable axes
- FAB for the screen's most important action, lower right on compact and medium, in the rail on expanded
- Large flexible top app bar that collapses on scroll, not a static header
- Moderate, consistent rounding from the shape scale (4, 8, 12, 16, 28dp). Not sharp, not everything a pill
- Ripple on every interactive surface

M3E replaced several components. Use the right-hand column in new work.

| No longer recommended | Use |
| --- | --- |
| Baseline navigation bar (80dp) | Flexible navigation bar, 64dp (`ShortNavigationBar`) |
| Baseline navigation rail (80dp) | Collapsed / expanded navigation rail, 96dp collapsed (`WideNavigationRail`) |
| Navigation drawer | Expanded navigation rail |
| Medium / large top app bar | Medium flexible (112dp) / large flexible (120dp) |
| Bottom app bar | Docked toolbar |
| Segmented button | Connected button group |
| Small FAB, speed dial, stacked FABs | FAB / medium FAB / large FAB, FAB menu |

**Figma frame, phone (412 × 915, compact):**
```
Frame: 412 × 915
  ├── Status Bar (transparent, content shows through)
  ├── Large flexible top app bar (120px, 152px with subtitle, collapses to 64px)
  ├── Content Area (extends behind both system bars, 16px side margins)
  ├── Navigation bar (64px)
  └── System Navigation (gesture bar or 3-button)
```

**Figma frame, tablet / unfolded foldable (840 × 1080, expanded):**
```
Frame: 840 × 1080
  ├── Status Bar
  ├── Navigation rail (96px wide collapsed, leading edge, full height)
  └── Content Area: two panes, 24px margins, 24px spacer between panes
```

System bar heights depend on the device and aren't in the Material spec. Take them from the Android UI kit in use.

**Wrong if** any signature item above is missing, or:
- Primary navigation is a row of tabs at the top
- Top-level destinations are reached by pushing screens instead of switching bar / rail destinations
- A navigation bar and a toolbar are on screen together
- A phone layout is stretched across a tablet

### Standing Rules

Every rule has a reason. If the reason doesn't apply, say so and proceed. Don't drop a rule silently.

- **Compose only.** I don't use XML layouts or Fragments in new code. `AndroidView` is for views with no Compose equivalent (maps, WebView, camera preview).
- **No colors outside the theme.** A `Color(0xFF...)` in a composable bypasses dynamic color, dark theme, and contrast levels at once.
- **No hardcoded dp/sp in composables.** Spacing, shape, type, and motion come from `MaterialTheme` or token objects.
- **Edge-to-edge and every window size.** The platform enforces both on current targets.
- **Springs for user-triggered motion**, from `MaterialTheme.motionScheme`. Duration-based `tween` only for system-triggered motion with no gesture behind it. Never linear for a UI transition. Token names beyond the scheme come from the `motion-design` skill.
- **Indeterminate waits of 200ms to 5s use `LoadingIndicator`.** Over 5s, a progress indicator. Under 200ms, nothing.
- **No deprecated APIs** when a replacement exists: `rememberRipple()` (use `ripple()`), `calculateWindowSizeClass()` and `currentWindowAdaptiveInfo()` (use `currentWindowAdaptiveInfoV2()`), `onBackPressed()`, Accompanist system UI controller, `ClickableText`, and from `material3` 1.5.0 the `Slider(value, onValueChange)` overloads (use `Slider(state, onValueChange)` with a `SliderState`).
- **I build custom.** When stock doesn't match the design, build the component. It still honors 48dp targets, semantics, ripple, theme tokens, and the motion scheme.
- **Measure before optimizing.** Recomposition counts in Layout Inspector, release build, mid-tier hardware.

### Ripple and State Layers

Material shows interaction state as a translucent layer of the content color over the component: 8% hovered, 10% focused, 10% pressed. In Compose the ripple draws it. `clickable`, `selectable`, `toggleable`, and every M3 component get it inside a Material theme with no code. Leave it alone unless the design specifies another indication.

To change it for one element, pass `ripple()` from `androidx.compose.material3`. `rememberRipple()` is deprecated and current Material components don't use it.

```kotlin
Box(
    modifier = Modifier
        .clip(MaterialTheme.shapes.medium)       // clip first so the ripple follows the shape
        .clickable(
            interactionSource = null,
            indication = ripple(color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.tertiary),
            onClick = onOpen
        )
)
```

A custom component that draws its own pressed state (shape morph, scale) keeps the ripple too, or supplies a custom `IndicationNodeFactory`. Never `indication = null` with nothing in its place.

### Haptics

Haptics confirm an outcome or mark a threshold. They aren't decoration, and they never fire on every tap. Use the semantic type. The system maps it to the right effect for the device and respects the user's haptics setting.

| Moment | `HapticFeedbackType` |
| --- | --- |
| Long-press recognized, drag picked up | `LongPress` |
| Action succeeded (save, send, payment) | `Confirm` |
| Action refused or failed validation | `Reject` |
| Switch or toggle changed | `ToggleOn` / `ToggleOff` |
| Slider or picker crossing a step | `SegmentTick` (`SegmentFrequentTick` for dense steps) |
| Drag crossed a commit threshold | `GestureThresholdActivate` |
| Gesture released and settled | `GestureEnd` |
| Text selection handle moved | `TextHandleMove` |

```kotlin
val haptic = LocalHapticFeedback.current
haptic.performHapticFeedback(HapticFeedbackType.Confirm)
```

Before adding a haptic to a stock M3 component, check on a device whether it already fires one.

### Touch Targets

At least 48 × 48dp (about 9mm), whatever the visual size. A 24dp icon carries 12dp of padding on each side. M3 components enforce it. Custom components use `Modifier.minimumInteractiveComponentSize()`, which expands the touch area without changing the visual.

### Semantics

Stock components fill in the accessibility tree. Custom ones have to state it.

```kotlin
// What it is and what state it is in
Modifier.toggleable(value = checked, role = Role.Switch, onValueChange = onCheckedChange)

// A row read as one item with one action
Modifier
    .clickable(onClickLabel = "Open thread", onClick = onOpen)
    .semantics(mergeDescendants = true) { }

// Section titles, so screen reader users can jump between them
Modifier.semantics { heading() }
```

- Use `clickable`, `toggleable`, and `selectable`, not raw pointer input. They supply role, state, focus, keyboard, and ripple together.
- Icons that carry meaning get a `contentDescription`. Decorative icons, and icons beside a label that says the same thing, get `null`.
- State goes in `stateDescription`, not in a rewritten label. Content that changes without user action is a `liveRegion`.
- Navigation destinations always keep their text labels.
- Everything interactive is reachable by keyboard. On tablets, foldables, and desktop windows a hardware keyboard is normal input.
- For custom components, assert semantics in tests (`assertIsToggleable`, `assertHasClickAction`). Screenshots don't catch these regressions.

### Contrast

| Content | Minimum against its background |
| --- | --- |
| Body text | 4.5:1 |
| Large text (18sp regular or 14sp bold and up), icons, graphics | 3:1 |
| Component containers and boundaries needed to identify a control | 3:1 |

M3 role pairs (`onPrimary` on `primary`, `onSurface` on `surface`) meet these in every scheme, dynamic color included. Hardcoded colors and mismatched pairs don't. That's the practical reason for the no-hardcoded-color rule. User-selected contrast levels are in theme-and-color.md.

### Text Scaling

Let the user's font size setting work. `heightIn(min = ...)`, not fixed heights, on anything holding text. Wrap, don't truncate, unless the full text is available elsewhere. Test at the largest font and display size on a compact window.
